title: This Fishing Game Was Made with AI? — Six AI-Assisted Games

scenes.title: Start with the games
lines: Hello, this is Yamyam Coding. Fishing, futuristic racing, and predicting a god's next attack: how much did AI contribute to making these games?
We'll look at six games, then examine the development milestones and tools their creators disclosed. We'll distinguish a rapidly built initial version from a game refined over several weeks.
Let's begin on this little island, where you can see beneath the water.

scenes.title: I Just Wanted to Fish
lines: I Just Wanted to Fish lets you explore an island and fish. A character casts from the beach, with fish and coral visible in the shallow water. Small crabs also wander along the shore.
The creator reported almost three weeks of work. That describes progress at the time of the post, not a completed commercial release.

The model was Claude Opus 5.5. Models and animation were made in Blender, then integrated into Unity 6. Connectors such as Blender MCP let AI operate production software instead of only replying in text.
The creator still designed the level, supplied reference drawings, and repeatedly reviewed and revised the models and motion. The character, water and environment had to work together.
The next example takes us from a 3D production pipeline into a small world in a browser.

scenes.title: Emberfall — Luminati
lines: This is Emberfall — Luminati. Its characters resemble pixel art, while the houses and paths occupy a space that can be viewed from different camera angles. It feels like a miniature village.
The public editor identifies Three.js and offers terrain-height, object and lighting controls. We could also verify character movement and camera rotation in the game.

The exact AI model version and total development time could not be confirmed from a creator primary source. A report about a quickly built initial version does not establish the development time of the whole current game.
From the impression of a small world, let's move to a project that keeps adding story and systems within one.

scenes.title: Nightshoal
lines: Nightshoal also features fishing and exploration, but has a different atmosphere. Waterways wind between cliffs and forests as a boat passes through. Its creator continues adding quests, story, fishing and inventory systems.
The public update marks week eleven of development. It uses Godot, with Claude Opus 5.5 in the latest work. Codex Astra had also been used earlier.

The workflow divides tasks among Tripo AI and Blender MCP for models, ElevenLabs for effects, and Stable Audio for music. Naming a tool does not mean every underlying model version has been disclosed.
Coordinating these tasks into one game matters. Someone must decide what to build, inspect the results and fix mismatches. The creator describes ongoing rework of the map and features.
Beyond building a world, there are also fast racing games that must respond immediately to player input.

scenes.title: VECTOR: Anti-Gravity Racing
lines: In VECTOR: Anti-Gravity Racing, floating craft replace wheels. You navigate corners, cross boost sections and race other craft.

The creator describes coding through AI conversation. The game uses Three.js and the browser graphics API WebGPU, with a WebGL 2 fallback. The creator also says AI was asked to use Blender for the models.
The exact development duration and model version could not be established from public evidence. We therefore cannot call it a three-day project or credit one specific latest model.
Just as interesting as high speed is its opposite: a game that pauses time and asks you to think through each move.

scenes.title: AUGURY: Duel of the Gods
lines: AUGURY features dueling gods, but it isn't about rapidly pressing buttons. Time pauses while you choose a move. A green silhouette previews your destination, and committing advances the outcome. Predicting the opponent's choice is central.

The development report identifies Phaser and TypeScript. DreamLayer and image-generation tools contributed characters, props and effects. The exact models and total development duration were not disclosed.

Generated images weren't automatically finished animation. Background removal, sizing, palette preparation, layer order and motion still needed work. The workflow turned generated artwork into readable game characters.
That need for refinement is worth remembering when we look at the next short development milestone.

scenes.title: Rally Road Rash
lines: Rally Road Rash features dirt-track collisions, jumps and rockets. Its creator reported making an initial version in about three days.

The workspace was Sandscape. The creator named Opus 5.5 for vehicles and physics and Astra 6 for visual refinement. Meshy supplied major vehicles and props, alongside simpler background geometry generated through code.

The creator edited levels personally and reported twenty-five years of experience. Motorcycle physics were still being refined. Three days describes that initial version; it doesn't guarantee anyone could achieve the same result in the same time.
Placed side by side, the six games reveal a change more clearly than their development-time numbers alone.

scenes.title: How far have things come?
lines: AI contributions now extend beyond code to models, images, animation work, sound and music. Some resulting games are available to interact with directly.
But 'made with AI' covers very different processes. The results make more sense when we ask which models were used, what they generated, and what people selected and revised.
This report is based on public material checked on October 18, 2026. Links to all six games and their development records will be in the description. Which one would you like to try?
